title: 1665 in London's burial records
hook: London's Bills of Mortality counted burials year by year. What did 1665 look like?

doesNotKnow: how a year's burials compare with normal
that the city's own weekly bills let us see it

misconception: Epidemics raise deaths a little; "the plague year" means somewhat more deaths than usual.
objective: The learner can say that London's recorded burials in 1665 were about six times the year before, mostly put down to plague, and that burials fell back the next year.

claims.text: London's Bills of Mortality recorded burials, plague burials and christenings by year, 1629-1710: 15,453 burials in 1664, 97,306 in 1665 (68,596 put down to plague), 12,738 in 1666; 9,972 christenings in 1665; 1636: 10,400 plague of 23,359.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: arbuthnot, Arbuthnot.csv, columns Mortality (burials), Plague, Males + Females (christenings). HistData Arbuthnot, columns Mortality and Plague (source not named in the documentation); christenings from Arbuthnot (1710). Copied into Demo.tsx as BILLS. The fact-checker should confirm against a printed Bill for 1665 if one can be opened.

claims.text: 1665's burials were 6.3 times the year before; 70% were put down to plague; the city buried about 10 people for every child christened (9.8).
claims.source: history-cycle1-check.mjs section 8: 97,306 / 15,453 = 6.30; 68,596 / 97,306 = 70.5% shown as Math.round = 70%; 97,306 / 9,972 = 9.8, rounded to 10 in the reveal. Demo.tsx computes the same values from BILLS. Stage readout for 1636 shows Math.round(44.52) = 45%.

claims.text: 1665 was the year of the Great Plague (question text).
claims.source: Context in the brief's stage question (cm-history, brief #8). Consistent with the Plague column (68,596 in 1665, the largest in the file). Common historical name; not separately sourced.

claims.text: Where it stops: these are recorded burials and recorded causes, not a count of every death or a doctor's diagnosis.
claims.source: What a Bill of Mortality records: burials and the cause written against them (brief #8). Brief: no held source sentence in the reveal; if the fact-checker wants a source for 'not a doctor's diagnosis', cut 'or a doctor's diagnosis'.

recall.question: A town normally records 100 deaths a year. One year it records 600, and 450 of those from one cause. What share is that cause?
recall.why: 450 of 600 is 75%: the share is out of that year's total, not the normal year's.
